title: url_holds_credential accepts a domain-user url with a password in the scp form, since the user part still bans every backslash
goal: kbcommon.url_holds_credential reads corp-backslash-user:password@host:path as a credential while a UNC path and a drive-letter path stay no credential, if the operator wants that shape refused
repro_reason: a decision-adjacent S3 of the SP-mut2pmu3 second review; the planted input is in the notes
notes: SP-mut2pmu3 second review gap 3 (S3, for the operator: it touches the credential rule they chose for BG-ouhonprv g1). kbcommon.py:688 bans a backslash in the user part, so a domain-user scp url holding a password (domain, backslash, user, colon, password, at, host, colon, path, built at run time) is no credential for url_holds_credential: a pointer or census url with it is accepted. The reviewer's fix if wanted: ban only a leading double backslash in the user part and keep the drive-letter test.
